title: DAY 42: at the first lull on or after the forty-second day Isao hoists a disco ball from the Stalheart's arm, the synth-wave track plays for forty-four seconds with the sector clock held, and the klaxon and the next wave end it
context: Owner, 2026-10-18: 'a silly celebration after 42 days. Entirely arbitrary, comic relief. Isao surprises us during a lull with a creation he made, a Disco Ball! 42 days surviving on this planet, Arthur would have been proud of us! bring your towel and let's party! cue in retro-synth wave music [44s_80s-retro-synth-wave.mp3] and a new disco ball asset from our team [SentryTowers_A6/stalheart-disco]. they party for a little bit and are interrupted by an alarm and yet another wave of monsters.' He chose a short cut followed by the party going on in the world over a whole-party cut (44 s without control) or no cut at all.
outcome: src/fx/disco-party.js, built with the story and torn down with it, ticked after storyBase.tick (a paused mixer action rewrites its nodes every update, so the pose must come after). The clock is pure (src/domain/disco-party-clock.js): armed when the day count reaches DAY_42.day and the sector loop is fighting and in a breath (sectorRun.breathing(): a pulse sector under breath.at of its last pulse, a flow sector under a quarter of its target) or secure, with no shot, seat or card, no wave warning counting down, the hull alive, not the arena, not won, Isao not mid-line; after DAY_42.patience (6) days without a breath, at the next free moment. The sequence: brief day_42 (glee: 'Forty-two days surviving on this planet. Arthur would have been proud of us.' / 'Bring your towel. Let's party!'), the track (day_42_music on a new music bus, through the loop handle and stopped at 43.8 s so it plays once; towers and tank ducked to 0.6), the sector clock held (createSectorRun clockHeld: the clock, gates and releases stand, pulseGap Infinity so the board's clock never arms, no stall counted); at 1.5 s the live cut discoReveal (10 s, skippable, a quarter orbit 70 m out and 28 m up round the extrusion tip, eased in 1.2 s; never over a seat or another shot); the arm to the diorama's crane-hook pose over 4 s with the Terraforming clip paused, the ball (a per-instance clone of the loader's cached scene, fetched two days ahead) hung at EXTRUSION_TIP - up * 6.2 m with its cradle hidden, the 16 s loop (pendulum, sphere spin, halo, laser ring, four floodlights in the diorama's colours, four additive laser quads) from src/domain/disco-celebration.js, a pure port of the owner's runtime; at 43.8 s the music stopped, danger_alert, the callout ALARM . CONTACT, brief day_42_over ('Party's over. They heard the bass.'), the next pulse armed through the board's own lead-in (armWave) if the sector is fighting, the lights gone, the ball lowered and shrunk away over 3 s, the clip resumed. Once a run. A hull death or the win mid-party ends it quietly; a pause longer than 0.3 s of wall time stops the track and ends the party at the alarm (the audio runs on while the game stands). Entries: ?day=42, the dev drawer's DAY 42 jump (sector 4), harness state day/party and partyNow(), browser step --day-42. The asset: assets/models/disco-ball/disco_ball_d0_lod1.glb vendored by scripts/import-disco-ball.mjs, pinned in docs/disco-ball-assets.lock.json and enforced by npm run assets:check; the track in assets/audio/day_42_music.mp3 (lazy, primed at day 40). The two lines are captions until the owner records voice-list section 14.
alternatives: The whole party as a frozen 44 s cut: cleaner as a scene, 44 s without control (the owner's earlier complaint about dead time).
No cut: the ball drops at the pole and the player looks if they want; easy to miss.
sfx.play for the track: returns no handle, so the party could not stop it; the loop handle stopped before the loop point plays it once.
A new releaseNow() in the sector loop: the board's own armWave gives the three-second warn rings and the same release path the stall safety uses.
Hiding the ball by detaching it from the loader's cached gltf.scene: a second party in the same page (regenerate) had no ball and no lights; a clone per instance instead.

Four dark spotlights kept for the whole run to avoid the shader relink at the cut: three.js evaluates zero-intensity spots per fragment and the crowd at the hull is already fill-bound; measured first instead.
evidence: test/disco-party-clock.mjs, test/disco-celebration.mjs, test/disco-party.mjs (a fake host: the sequence, the hold, the hull-death cut, the shared cached scene, a failed load, restore()), test/sector-run.mjs (clockHeld, breathing())
